svg.title: Macular degeneration and the other patterns of vision loss
svg.desc: The same scene shown four times: normally, with macular degeneration blanking the centre, with glaucoma closing in from the edges, and with a cataract clouding the whole field. Then an Amsler grid drawn straight and drawn warped, which is the sign of the wet form. Below, dry versus wet macular degeneration.
svg.text: WHICH PART OF THE PICTURE GOES
Macular degeneration takes the middle. Glaucoma takes the edges. A cataract fogs the lot.
She can still cross a room but cannot read or recognise a face → macular degeneration.
She reads fine but keeps bumping into door frames → glaucoma. That functional split is how
✅ THE AMSLER GRID — how she catches the change at home
Cover one eye. Stare at the centre dot.
Any square that is wavy, blurred or missing
Wavy straight lines — door frames, tiles, text —
is metamorphopsia, and it means the WET form.
Caught early it is treatable with anti-VEGF
injections. This is how the change gets caught.
macular cells thin; drusen build up
